result.topic_en: Series reversion: a power series y = αx + βx² + γx³ + … is set up, the powers 1/x, 1/x², 1/x³ are written as Laurent series in x with unknown coefficients, and x, x², x³ are expressed as power series in y whose coefficients are related to those coefficients (a Lagrange-type inversion).
result.transcription:
No. Monath Litt. G.
57 [-75-]
$X = \alpha x + \beta xx + \gamma x^3 \ldots\ldots = y$
$\frac{1}{X} = \frac{a'}{x} + b' + c'xx + \partial' x^3 \ldots$
$\frac{1}{X^2} = \frac{a''}{x^2} + \frac{b''}{x} + c'' + d''x +$
$\frac{1}{X^3} = \frac{a'''}{x^3} + \frac{b'''}{xx} + \frac{c'''}{x} + d''' + \text{etc}$
etc.
$x = a'y + \frac{1}{2}b''yy + \frac{1}{3}c'''y^3 + \text{etc.}$
$xx = a''yy + \frac{2}{3}b'''y^3 + \frac{2}{4}c''''y^4 + \text{etc}$
$x^3 = a'''y^3 + \frac{3}{4}b''''y^4 + \frac{3}{5}c^{v}y^5 + \text{etc}$

methods.what: Setting up a power series y = X(x) for reversion
Laurent expansions of negative powers 1/X^n in x with undetermined coefficients
Series reversion (Lagrange inversion): coefficients of x^n as a power series in y are n/(n+k) times the corresponding coefficients of the Laurent expansions of 1/X^(n+k)
Inversion formula applied to x² and x³
